explain.title: The goal
explain.text: Adding fractions is easy when the pieces are the same size. 1/4 + 1/4? That's 2/4. Done. But 2/3 + 1/4 has thirds and quarters, which are different-sized pieces, so you can't add them yet. The goal: make the pieces the same size, then add.

explain.title: The method: 4 moves
explain.say: Here's the method. Four small moves.
steps: Match the bottoms. Find a number that both bottom numbers fit into. (That's called the common denominator.)
Convert. Rewrite each fraction so it has that new bottom.
Add the tops. The bottom stays the same.
Simplify. Can the answer be made smaller? If yes, do it.

explain.title: The golden rule
explain.say: One rule makes the converting work.
explain.text: Whatever you do to the bottom, do the same to the top. That keeps the fraction's value the same, just cut into smaller slices.
explain.tip: To find a common bottom, multiply the two bottoms. For 3 and 4 that's 12. It always works.

lines.say: Let's add these. Thirds and quarters don't match, so step 1: match the bottoms.
Multiply the bottoms: 3 × 4 = 12. Both fit into 12, so that's our new bottom.
To turn 3 into 12, we multiply by 4. Same on top: 2 × 4 = 8.
To turn 4 into 12, we multiply by 3. Same on top: 1 × 3 = 3.
Same-sized pieces now! Add the tops: 8 + 3 = 11. The bottom stays 12.
Last check: can anything divide both 11 and 12? No, so we're done.

steps.correctSay: Yes! 2/5 = 8/20 and 1/4 = 5/20, so 8 + 5 = 13. Nothing divides both 13 and 20, so 13/20 is as simple as it gets.
